articleTitle: Development and Characterization of 3D Electronic Printed Gold Nanoparticle-based Sensing Electrodes with Potential for Environmental and Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), one of the techniques for electrochemical analysis, has been used for a wide range of applications especially chemical- and bio-sensing. Here, we present a methodology for the fabrication of gold nanoparticle-based flexible EIS electrodes that can be used for environmental and biomedical applications. These sensing electrodes are fabricated by processing functional nanoparticle ink via an advanced 3D electronic printer known as the aerosol jet printer which can achieve high resolution and compatible with a wide range of substrates. In this work, we investigated printing both gold nanoparticle ink and polyimide dielectric ink to realize a fully printed EIS sensing electrodes. Besides, we looked into utilizing a surface treatment for improving film adhesion to the substrate and conducted various tests to evaluate the reliability and the performance of the printed gold electrodes.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Full-thickness Skin Tissue Models Using Gelatin-based Hydrogel Sponges with Continuous Micropores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Skin models fabricated using hydrogels have attracted much attention as new tools for drug penetration tests and regenerative medicine. However, conventional skin models do not have inner continuous micropores that function as vascular networks, and there remain challenges in efficiently supplying oxygen and nutrients to cells inside the hydrogels. In this study, we proposed a new strategy to create full-thickness skin models with continuous micropores in the dermis layer utilizing a bicontinuous aqueous two-phase dispersion consisting of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-rich phase and photo-crosslinkable gelatin (GelMA)-rich phase. The GelMA-rich phase was selectively photo-crosslinked to form hydrogel sponges with continuous micropores. The volume ratio of the two phases was examined as a key factor dominating the morphology and continuity of the micropores. We created skin models encapsulating normal human dermal fibroblasts in the hydrogel sponges as the dermis and with a layer of human keratinocytes as the epidermis. The presented approach to the formation of skin models is effective because the continuous micropores in the dermal layer function as vascular networks, efficiently supplying oxygen and nutrients to the cells in the skin tissue models.

articleTitle: Developing a Respiratory Pressure Simulation Platform for a Portable Negative Pressure Filtering Chest Drainage System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: This study aims to reduce the risk of aerosol infection in patients and healthcare workers by establishing a portable negative pressure filtering chest drainage system (PNPFCDS) that filters aerosols and microparticles. By controlling the negative pressure precisely, the system can prevent aerosol transmission under different air leaks. By using a respiratory pressure simulation platform (RPSP), it has been demonstrated that the negative pressure filtering chest drainage system can achieve a minimum measured pressure error of 1.6% without simulated intrapleural pressure changes when the air leak flow rises to 800 ml/min. When the target pressure is −1.5 kPa under simulated intrapleural pressure changes with air leak of 500 ml/min, the measured pressure change rate ranges from −16.7 % to +22.7%. When the target pressure is −9 kPa, the measured pressure change rates ranges from −2% to +6.7%. According to ISO 10079-1, this study provides a model of a negative pressure filtering chest drainage system that is effective and safe.

articleTitle: Scalable Fabrication of Nano-yarn-based Strain Sensor for Motion Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Nanomaterials have gained significant attention in fabricating on-skin and wearable electronic devices, offering diverse applications in interactive touch screens, pressure sensors, strain sensors, and medical devices. Researchers have explored stretchable conductive fibers embedded in soft polymers for their lightweight, flexible nature and fabric attachment capabilities. Various natural materials, including flax, cotton, wool, and silk, have created flexible sensors. High conductivity in natural materials can be achieved through carbonization or coating processes using conductive particles like graphene, carbon nanotubes, and liquid metal. However, these processes have drawbacks such as elevated working temperatures, complex setups, lengthy durations, and labor-intensive procedures. The dipping coating technique, while promising, also faces challenges in achieving precise thickness control, uniform particle coverage, and proper adhesion for long-term durability. This study introduces an automated machine and a layer-by-layer dip coating approach to address these challenges in fabricating polyurethane yarn (PUY)-based strain sensors. The novel technique significantly reduces production time, increases success rates, and demonstrates the potential for efficient and scalable fabrication of PUY-based strain sensors.

articleTitle: Hydrogel Beads-Templated Emulsification-based Droplet Digital PCR of Targeted Genome Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Low-cost and convenient methodologies to produce uniform droplets are demanded for the detection and quantification of environmental DNA (eDNA). In this work, we demonstrate that hydrogel-beads templated emulsification is applicable to generate monodispersed droplets within one minute via vortexing and pipetting. Compartmentalized reactions via the beads-templated digital PCR (bdPCR) have been further conducted to amplify the targeted region of a seahorse species genome. The results from bdPCR have shown a similar limit of detection compared with the traditional water-in-oil based droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). SYBR green staining results further demonstrated the successful amplification of target templates through bdPCR. Finally, the bdPCR platform was adopted to amplify eDNA from marine water and the results showcased the successful detection of a seahorse species.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Migration of Neutrophil-Like Cells under a pH Gradient using a Microfluidic Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Neutrophils are known to accumulate in an acidified inflammatory microenvironment, but the effects of environmental factors on neutrophils are not fully understood. Here, we investigated the response of neutrophil-like differentiated human promyelocytic leukemia cells (HL-60) to pH changes. A previously developed microfluidic device that enables control of the oxygen concentration was used to control the pH in a microenvironment. The CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration in the cell culture medium was controlled by gas exchange between the media and gas channels, thereby establishing certain pH gradients based on chemical equilibrium. The device enabled the generation of a pH 8.5 to 7.1 gradient when gas mixtures of 1% and 50% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were supplied to the left and right gas channels, respectively. Neutrophil-like differentiated HL-60 cells were then seeded into the media channels to observe their cellular dynamics under the pH gradient. Quantitative evaluation showed that cell migration was suppressed in the low-pH (high CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration) region compared to the high-pH (low CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration) region, whereas no clear chemotactic migration in response to pH was observed.

articleTitle: Wrist Motion Classification Using Flexible sEMG Sensors in Different Feature Conditions Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) is a bioelectrical signal to reflect human intention before actual motion occurs. EMG has been widely used in human-machine interaction such as robot control, rehabilitation and health monitoring. In this work, we have designed an intelligent approach for wrist motion classification based on EMG signals. Since commercial electrodes cannot maintain good contact with skin during deformation, we have utilized a new type of fabricated flexible electrodes. With these electrodes, high-quality signals can be acquired. And the machine learning methods have been utilized to classify the extracted feature sets. Four different feature conditions have been compared. In the condition of six EMG features, we have identified four wrist gestures including wrist flexion, extension, radial deviation, and ulnar deviation with the best accuracy of 92.26%.

articleTitle: Highly efficient mRNA transfection with droplet cell squeezing for cellular engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: We present a novel droplet-based intracellular delivery platform for mRNA transfection. The platform leverages the use of two immiscible fluids to encapsulate a cell and external cargos within a single droplet. The formed droplets travel a narrow z-axis stepwise constriction, smaller than the cell diameter, exerting a physical opening of the cell membrane. Consequently, the platform enables highly effective internalization of cargo into the cell through a combination of diffusive and convective flow. The presented microfluidic approach offers high mRNA transfection efficiency (>98%) with nearly clog-free operation. These results highlight the platform’s potential as a next-generation microfluidics-based intracellular delivery system, showcasing its capacity to achieve both exceptional delivery efficiency and high-throughput capabilities for cell therapy applications.

articleTitle: A novel antifouling layer for cardiac troponin I detection in a blood sample
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: The impurity in the blood sample solution is the leading cause of noise in biosensors. This work investigates the effect of a novel antifouling layer consisting of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), cross-linked bovine serum albumin (BSA), and mercaptoethanol. The AuNPs are deposited through the electrodeposition technique in order to create a low-cost conductive layer with an enormous surface area. Then, a BSA and Glutaraldehyde (GA) are mixed and incubated on the AuNPs layer. The resulting surface becomes a porous layer which plays an important role in protecting the detection layer from contaminants in the sample solution. This work enables the feasible and cost-effective LOC for cTnI detection. The limit of detection of 0.097 pg/mL is obtained with a rapid detection time of 10 minutes.

articleTitle: Point of Care Electrochemical Aptasensor for Early Screening of Pancreatic Cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC), one of the highest causes of mortality, has a poor prognosis. Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is the most frequent pancreatic tumor. Lack of pre-screening and early diagnosis procedures contributes to the high fatality rate. Even though, the identifiable cancer tumors are removed, metastasis makes treatment more difficult. CT, MRI, endoscopic ultrasonography, and peripheral blood biomarkers are the main PC diagnostic modalities. Despite advances in diagnosis, only 20% of pancreatic tumors are detected at early stage and can be removed surgically. To overcome this, researchers think blood biomarkers may offer early PC detection. One of the most important biomarkers for early PC diagnosis is mucin. MUC1, MUC4, MUC5AC, and MUC16 are highly upregulated in pancreatic cancer. MUC1 is a fundamental component of healthy pancreatic ductal cells and is aberrantly expressed in pancreatic cancer cells. MUC1 activates cellular and humoral immune responses to tumor epitopes. MUC1 is expressed in approximately 90% of pancreatic cancer patients, making it a better biomarker than serum CA-199, CA125, AFP, and CEA. Point of care (POC) diagnostics are essential for reaching greater populations for improved healthcare and early diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. Biomarker detection using electrochemical sensors allows POC diagnosis that is sensitive, selective, and miniaturized for field testing. This study uses Cadmium Telluride (CdTe) quantum dots and aptamer to detect mucin with sensitivity upto 10 ng/mL electrochemically.

articleTitle: Assessing Lower Limb Movement Performance in Elderly Individuals Using a Nanocomposite E-Textile Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: The knee joint is one of the most important joints in our lower body, affecting humans’ lower limb activities. For instance, the knee joint can even bear three to four times the human body’s weight when running and climbing. The knee joint is prone to degenerative lesions for older people as they age, which significantly affects their daily lives. Therefore, long-term and real-time assessment of lower-limb motions in older people is crucial for their lower-limb health detection. In this work, we developed wearable knee sensors based on nanocomposite e-textile strain sensors for detecting knee joints’ range of motion (ROM) while older people perform lower-limb activities. A total of ten features were extracted to characterize their STS performance by detecting their knee joint range of motion through normal speed and fast speed sit-to-stand (STS). The elderly subjects were grouped by their age, gender, and body mass index (BMI) to assess the relationship of these three parameters with the extracted features. As a result, the stability, ROM, and gender of elderly subjects while performing fast speed STS had a significant relationship with age and BMI (P<0.05). The result demonstrates the generalizability of e-textile sensors for assessing lower-limb motions, which shows great potential for long-term and real-time detection of lower-limb health in older people.

articleTitle: Functionalized ZnO Nanowires for Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the immobilization of carboxylic acid moieties on the surface of ZnO and silicon nanowires and its potential for biosensing applications. We functionalize ZnO and Si nanowires that were synthesized with the CVD technique. We use spectroscopic techniques to determine the nature of bonding and orientation of oleic acid molecules at the nanowire surface, which is used as a model system. Furthermore, based on photoluminescence data on modified and unmodified ZnO nanowires with oleic acid, we propose a generic approach to sense biomolecules along with a mechanism of sensing.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Segmentation of Embryo Inner Cell Mass and Trophectoderm Epithelium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Embryologists commonly assess the viability of embryos for in vitro fertilization using the Gardner blastocyst grading system, which focuses on the inner cell mass (ICM) and trophectoderm epithelium (TE) regions. To overcome the difficulties in classifying these regions due to similarities in texture and appearance, this paper demonstrates the use of ResUNet-50, a deep learning neural network model. With ResUNet-50, the ICM region was segmented with a 99.8% accuracy, 98.7% precision, 98.7% recall, 98.7% Sørensen-Dice coefficient, and 98.6% Jaccard Index. ResUNet-50 also segmented the TE region with a 98.2% accuracy, 92.4% precision, 90.3% recall, 91.2% Sørensen-Dice coefficient, and 91.3% Jaccard Index.

articleTitle: PCB-based Mass-produced EGFET pH Sensor with Electroplated Reference Electrode for Daily Saliva Acidity Monitoring in Mouth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: A high performance pH sensor chip with integrated reference electrode on a mass-producible printed circuit board (PCB) is developed for directly measuring saliva pH level in mouth. Commercially available indium-tin-oxide (ITO) thin film and the on-PCB electroplated Ag/AgCl reference electrode are utilized for detecting the hydrogen ions under an extended gate field effect transistor scheme. To produce flat AgCl on the reference electrode surface, silver plating is performed using homemade silver electroplating solution, followed by chemical chlorination using FeCl3. The integrated sensor chip exhibit excellent sensitivity (84.6 mV/pH), good linearity (R2=0.9999), and rapid response time (< 2 s) for pH measurement. It facilitates easy monitoring of saliva pH before and after meals, supporting daily oral health care.

articleTitle: Accuracy Enhancement of Micro-PMV Sensor System for Human Thermal Comfort Measurements through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based method to significantly improve the accuracy of micro-PMV (Predicted Mean Vote) sensor system for Human Thermal Comfort (HTC) measurements. According to the analysis, an accurate prediction of metabolic rate is critical to determine reliable PMV values. Therefore, compared to the previous work, we have divided indoor human activities into more categories (9 vs 3) which cover a wider range of typical indoor scenarios to address the limitation of metabolic rate estimation. A Random Forest ML model was trained based on a 6-axis MEMS motion sensor data (acceleration and angular velocity) to achieve an impressive accuracy of 94.29% in the classified human activities. This approach significantly improves the event diversity for better accuracy of metabolic rate prediction, resulting in better performance of PMV-based HTC assessment. Thus, this work provides the foundation to develop a new ML-enabled micro PMV sensor system to be integrated for smart energy-efficient buildings to reduce carbon footprint in the era of AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things).

articleTitle: GQD as a probe and Graphene Oxide (GO)-Au/Ag nanocarriers for faster and more sensitive E. coli and S. aureus detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) are a distinct class of quantum dots that demonstrate notable electro-catalytic capabilities. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the properties of graphene quantum dots (GQDs) and compare them to semiconductor quantum dots (CdSe QDs) in order to evaluate GQD’s potential as highly sensitive agents for the detection of bacteria. Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus are recognized as the predominant pathogens responsible for causing diseases worldwide. Failure to immediately diagnose and treat these pathogens can lead to severe and sometimes devastating outcomes. In this study, the sensing platform utilises Screen-Printed Carbon Electrodes (SPCE) that have been modified with Graphene Oxide/gold nanoparticles (GO-AuNP) and Graphene Oxide/silver composite nanoparticles (GO-AgNP). Furthermore, we utilised electrochemical (EC) probes in conjunction with co-reactants, namely nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (N-GQDs) and cadmium selenide quantum dots (CdSe QDs). The incorporation of graphene oxide-gold nanoparticle (GO-AuNP) and graphene oxide-silver nanoparticle (GO-AgNP) nanocomposites has been observed to enhance the stability and amplification capabilities of the biosensor. By employing this methodology, it is possible to rapidly detect pathogens in real samples even at concentrations as low as 1 CFU/mL.

articleTitle: The Mid-Infrared Region Absorption of Graphene-based Photodetector with Au-grating Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice, has garnered immense attention for its exceptional electrical conductivity, transparency, and mechanical strength. These properties make graphene an ideal candidate for photodetectors, as it can efficiently convert incident photons into electrical signals. The integration of graphene into surface plasmonic devices has opened up new avenues for photodetection technology. In our research, we combine graphene and surface plasmonic devices to realize a high responsivity mid-infrared graphene photodetector with a grating metal/graphene/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> structure. The Bruker Vertex70 Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) was used for the mid-infrared spectrum measurement. With different linewidth of Au grating structure, the peak of absorption redshifts as the grating linewidth increases and the intensity is also different. Further, by adding graphene, the total absorption increases. Due to these advantages, the Au-grating graphene device can be used as infrared photodetectors.

articleTitle: The Impact of Oxygen Concentration on Interactions between Breast Cancer Cells and the Vascular Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Cancer cells can metastasize from the primary tumor to other organs by invading blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. The hypoxic conditions generated in a tumor microenvironment influence the growth of the cancer. However, few studies have focused on the interaction between cancer cells and the vascular network under different oxygen concentrations, a shortcoming that this study sought to address. In the experiments described here, breast cancer cells and cells that form the vascular networks (vascular endothelial cells and fibroblasts) were co-cultured in different channels in a microfluidic device, while controlling the oxygen concentration. We observed that growth of the cancer cells was strongly affected by the interaction with the vascular network, such that the number of cells migrating toward the vascular network increased under hypoxic conditions compared to the atmospheric oxygen concentration. Additionally, angiogenesis from the vascular network was observed under hypoxia with little change in the growth of the cancer cells.

articleTitle: Gas Chromatography System with A Modular Gas Sensor for the Regeneration of Sensor Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: We developed a headspace gas chromatography system (GC-MOX) composed of a modular metal oxide gas sensor, assembled from a commercially available sensor, a tube of temperature-controlled adsorption polymer 2,6-diphenylphenol (Tenax TA), an air pump, and a solenoid valve. The system was shown to discriminate up to four volatile organic compounds (VOC) species by the elution volume between Tenax TA and VOCs. The system was shown to record the sensor response for at least 200 consecutive rounds of exposure to VOCs. The embedded heating capacity was shown to be effective in restoring the sensor sensitivity by 1.8-fold.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation for Water Sensing System of Unmanned Surface Mobile Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Fish and shrimp virus infection, water acidification, cold and heat waves are common problems in traditional aquaculture industry. In order to reduce the loss of aquaculture, it is necessary to develop smart aquaculture through various water quality sensors, internet of things(IoT) and information communication technology, and big data analysis. However, today’s smart aquaculture monitoring technology still cannot meet the needs of the aquaculture industry, because many water quality environmental parameters are controlled by IoT companies, and the network costs derived from the maintenance of water quality sensors and large amounts of data are borne by the aquaculture industry. Besides, he traditional monitoring of water quality parameters cannot immediately reflect the current water quality of the aquafarm. In view of this, it is practical and valuable to develop a water sensing system of unmanned surface mobile vehicle(WSSUSMV).The WSSUSMV proposed in this paper is equipped with four water quality sensors(including dissolved oxygen, pH, water temperature, and oxidation-reduction potentiometer). It can not only make up for the lack of real-time monitoring of water quality at fixed points in the aquafarm, but also monitor and upload water quality parameters in real time through the IoT device. In addition, we have also designed a special webpage to graph the sensing values, and provide users with real-time viewing of the water quality dynamics of the aquafarm through mobile devices or remote computers. The results in this paper can help to improve the overall efficiency, success rate and income of the aquafarm at the level of intelligent control.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Gold Nanoformulations for Prostate Cancer Drug Delivery Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: This work describes the development of a novel prostate cancer treatment using docetaxel-encapsulated gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) for drug delivery applications. The functionalization of gold nanoparticles with docetaxel is attracting the interest of researchers in nanomedicine because of its advantageous surface flexibility, stability, and good optical qualities. They are the appropriate vehicle for targeted and selective drug delivery to prostate cancer due to their inherent characteristics. The chemical reduction process was used to create AuNPs with a size of 4.5nm, which were then functionalized with polyethylene glycol, folic acid, and docetaxel. Various techniques were used to explore the major physicochemical properties of gold nanoformulations (AuNFs). The AuNFs encapsulation efficiency was determined to be 93%. The AuNFs In-vitro drug release profile was observed in three different kinetic patterns, which mainly follow the Higuchi kinetics. In-vitro cytotoxicity and fluorescence labeling analyses were used to determine the apoptotic quantification and binding affinity (IC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>) of the AuNFs against the prostate cancer cell line (PC3).

articleTitle: Multi-view Classifier and Fast Brain Tumor Segmentation Using Geometric Fast Data Density Functional Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: The article proposed a new architecture for fast brain tumor image segmentation based on their intrinsic geometric properties using the geometric fast data density functional transform (g-fDDFT). The g-fDDFT, as a feature pre-extractor, utilized the structure of AutoEncoder to provide global convolutions on images for extracting global features. It also exploited the geometric properties of energy landscapes offered by functional operations to reduce the computational costs caused by convolutional operations efficiently. Under the g-fDDFT framework, the computational complexity would reduce from $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ to $\mathcal{O}(n\,\text{log}\, n)$. To verify its performance on tasks of brain tumor image segmentation and the recognition of oriented views of MRI data, we employed open-access resources from BraTS 2020 and clinical image datasets. We also used the U-Net, 3D-Unet, D-UNet, and nnU-Net as our backbone models for tumor segmentation. Experimental results validated that the training and inference time using the proposed g-fDDFT significantly reduced by 57% and 52%, respectively, compared to that using the naïve D-UNet. Meanwhile, the accuracy estimations of brain tumor image segmentation had comparable results between the backbone models and utilizing the g-fDDFT. The geometric multi-view classifier also benefited the recognition and segmentation of tumor and necrotic/peritumoral edema images of the clinical dataset. The capability of selecting tumor candidates and fast labeling also exhibits the exclusive performance of g-fDDFT. Its flexibility and corresponding physical constraints also reveal the possibility of model extension.
